stances_toward.note: The Islamic State's Khorasan Province (ISKP) is the Emirate's declared mortal enemy and the UN Monitoring Team calls it the Taliban's main adversary; Muttaqi named ISIS the main regional threat in Delhi in October 2025 and Lavrov credited the Emirate's anti-IS record in October 2026. The UN's 16th report says the threat is 'suppressed, although not eliminated'. nsa-isis is the parent organisation, ISKP is its province; the stub has no Khorasan seat. Bond - grievance: ISKP attacks on Taliban officials and its denunciation of Chinese interests.

stances_toward.note: A mortal enemy in the ontology's sense: the group aims to destroy the Iraqi state and its Shia-led order, and the state's declared aim is its elimination (al-Zaidi on 1 October: the end of the coalition 'does not mean the end of our battle with terrorism'). Capacity is much reduced, but ISIS has been more active around Kirkuk and the disputed areas, including a deadly attack on a police unit in late September or early October 2026, and Iraq is now holding thousands of detainees moved from Syria. Chatham House's Rodgers judges a major resurgence unlikely but the threat real. Bond - grievance: 2014 and the Mosul and Sinjar atrocities.

stances_toward.note: Adversary through actions: the SDF defeated the caliphate at Raqqa (2017) and Baghuz (2019), guarded up to 7,000 ISIS prisoners and the al-Hol camp for years, and ISIS cells keep attacking it. The weakness is not hostility but custody: its prisons and camp were taken over by Damascus, the UN and the US-led transfer to Iraq within a month (Shaddadi: about 120 escapees by the interior ministry, 1,500 by the SDF). The SDF no longer holds the means for the fight. Bond - grievance (the 2014-19 war).

stances_toward.note: The one mortal enemy in this card: ISIS seeks the destruction of the new state and its leaders and the new state's declared aim is the elimination of the group. Damascus joined the counter-ISIS coalition (10 Nov 2025, the 90th member), took over the al-Hol camp and prisons in January 2026 and saw more than 5,700 ISIS detainees moved to Iraq by US forces (21 Jan - 12 Feb 2026), and works with US, French, British and Jordanian strikes (Hawkeye Strike, 10 Jan 2026) after the Palmyra attack of 13 Dec 2025 (Syria's interior ministry said the gunman was a security-force member due for dismissal). The group still holds ground beyond Damascus's reach (Bloomberg Government, February 2026). Bond - grievance.

relations_to.summary: The UN Monitoring Team's 16th report (December 2025) says the Taliban have 'suppressed, although not eliminated' ISKP and describes it as the movement's main adversary; ISKP's capability was degraded by Taliban and Pakistani counter-terrorism. The 38th report (S/2026/651) notes the Islamic State at a lower ebb after leadership losses including its deputy leader's death in May 2026.

relations_to.summary: 19-20 Jan 2026: the SDF loses control of Shaddadi prison, which held thousands of ISIS prisoners, as the army advances; the interior ministry counts about 120 escapees (81 recaptured), the SDF 1,500, and each side accuses the other of engineering the break. On 20 Jan the SDF withdraws from al-Hol (23,000+ residents at end-2025) citing 'international indifference'; the UN takes over the camp on 22 Jan and the last residents are moved out by 22 Feb.
